## `check_blueprint_errors`

*Read-only.*

Check a blueprint for compilation errors, warnings, structural issues, and orphaned nodes. Read-only: it does NOT recompile the Blueprint (it reports the cached Status).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_path` | string | yes | Object path, package path, or bare short name of the blueprint (resolved via mcp_common::ResolveAssetFlexible; ambiguity errors out listing candidates) |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_path: string, resolved_object_path: string, blueprint_class: string, is_blueprint: bool, error_status: string, error_message: string, errors: [string], warnings: [string], error_count: int, warning_count: int, blueprint_compiled: bool, compilation_status: string, is_static_analysis: bool, recompiled_blueprint: bool, orphaned_node_heuristic: string }`

## `list_validators`

*Read-only.*

List the editor data validators the DataValidation subsystem has enabled (ForEachEnabledValidator): class_name, class_path and enabled for each, plus validator_count. Read-only; errors when the DataValidation plugin subsystem is unavailable. validate_asset runs them on one asset.

No parameters.

**Returns:** `{ validators: [{ class_name: string, class_path: string, enabled: bool }], validator_count: number }`

## `profile_blueprint_execution`

*Destructive.*

STATIC complexity analysis of a blueprint (node/function/variable counts + heuristic score). It does NOT profile any runtime execution. WARNING, SIDE EFFECT: by default it RECOMPILES the Blueprint purely to time the compile, which marks the asset dirty and can surface new compile errors on an asset you only meant to READ -- pass compile_for_timing=false for a genuinely read-only analysis. Three response fields are misnamed and each is flagged as such in the payload: `execution_time` is the COMPILE time in ms, `cpu_usage` is the heuristic complexity score (not CPU), and `memory_usage` is the .uasset size on disk (not memory).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_path` | string | yes | Object path, package path, or bare short name of the blueprint (resolved via mcp_common::ResolveAssetFlexible; ambiguity errors out listing candidates) |
| `compile_for_timing` | boolean | no | Optional (default true): recompile the Blueprint to measure compile time. Pass false for a pure read-only analysis (execution_time/compilation_score_ms then report 0). |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_path: string, resolved_object_path: string, blueprint_class: string, execution_time: number, memory_usage: int, cpu_usage: number, performance_rating: string, profile_status: string, total_nodes: int, function_count: int, event_count: int, variable_count: int, component_count: int, complexity_score: number, memory_score_mb: number, compilation_score_ms: number, blueprint_compiled: bool, is_static_analysis: bool, runtime_profiled: bool, recompiled_blueprint: bool, execution_time_is_compile_time_ms: bool, cpu_usage_is_complexity_score: bool, memory_usage_is_disk_file_size_bytes: bool, under_readonly_root: bool, side_effects: [string], recommendations?: [string] }`

## `run_map_check`

*Destructive.*

Run editor Map Check on the current level and report message counts, each message resolved back to the actor/component the engine attached to it.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `check_deprecated_only` | boolean | no | When true, only run deprecated-asset checks (optional, default false) |
| `base_libraries` | array | no | Package roots to classify each message's class against (optional, default: the project's Read Only Content Roots). An explicit [] disables the classification. Reported as data in class_root/class_root_is_base_library; the tool never judges which root is "upstream". |

**Returns:** `{ world: string, map_check_ran: bool, check_deprecated_only: bool, base_libraries: [string], error_count: number, warning_count: number, info_count: number, total_messages: number, messages_truncated: bool, messages: [{ severity: number, text: string, token_source: string, object_path: string, object_resolved: bool, actor_name: string, actor_label: string, actor_path: string, actor_class: string, actor_guid: string, component_name: string, class_asset_path: string, class_root: string, class_root_is_base_library: bool }] }`

## `test_blueprint_function`

*Destructive.*

Static analysis of one function graph of a blueprint (node/pin counts + heuristics). WARNING: it does NOT execute the function; it RECOMPILES the Blueprint (FKismetEditorUtilities::CompileBlueprint) and reports the COMPILE time as `execution_time`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_path` | string | yes | Object path, package path, or bare short name of the blueprint (resolved via mcp_common::ResolveAssetFlexible; ambiguity errors out listing candidates) |
| `function_name` | string | yes | Name of the function graph to analyze within the blueprint |
| `compile_for_timing` | boolean | no | Optional (default true): recompile the Blueprint to measure compile time. Pass false to skip the recompile side effect (execution_time then reports 0). |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_path: string, resolved_object_path: string, function_name: string, test_success: bool, test_result: string, execution_time: number, memory_usage: int, node_count: int, connection_count: int, performance_rating: string, function_exists: bool, blueprint_compiled: bool, is_static_analysis: bool, function_was_executed: bool, recompiled_blueprint: bool, execution_time_is_compile_time_ms: bool, memory_usage_is_disk_file_size_bytes: bool, connection_count_is_pin_count: bool, under_readonly_root: bool, issues?: [string] }`

## `trace_blueprint_execution`

*Read-only.*

STATIC listing of a blueprint's graphs and their nodes. It does NOT trace anything at runtime, despite the name: `trace_status` reports "StaticAnalysisOnly", and `total_execution_paths` does NOT count execution paths -- it counts GRAPHS, kept under that name only for compatibility, alongside the honest alias `graphs_analyzed` and the flag `total_execution_paths_is_graph_count`. Collapsed composite subgraphs are invisible unless you pass include_composites=true. TO ACTUALLY OBSERVE RUNTIME use set_blueprint_breakpoint (+ PIE) or watch_pie_property instead.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_path` | string | yes | Object path, package path, or bare short name of the blueprint (resolved via mcp_common::ResolveAssetFlexible; ambiguity errors out listing candidates) |
| `include_composites` | boolean | no | Optional (default false): also descend into collapsed composite subgraphs (UEdGraph::SubGraphs). Macro-instance graphs are NOT followed (they usually live in another Blueprint / an engine macro library). |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_path: string, resolved_object_path: string, blueprint_class: string, trace_status: string, trace_level: string, trace_message: string, file_size_bytes: int, file_size_mb: number, total_execution_paths: int, graphs_analyzed: int, total_execution_paths_is_graph_count: bool, is_static_analysis: bool, traced_runtime: bool, includes_composite_subgraphs: bool, limitations: [string], function_count: int, event_count: int, execution_flow: [string], function_calls: [string], event_calls: [string], blueprint_compiled: bool, compilation_status: string }`

## `watch_pie_property`

*Destructive.*

Sample one or SEVERAL properties across a PIE session, arming BEFORE PIE starts so a write that happens in BeginPlay is still observable. Answers "what did this value do during play", NOT "who wrote it": it SAMPLES rather than intercepting writes, so `identifies_writer` is always false and a transient A->B->A between two samples is invisible. THE ORDER MATTERS: action="start" arms and returns immediately (it cannot block the game thread), THEN you start PIE, and afterwards action="status" returns the recorded samples. Arming while PIE is ALREADY running is honoured but flagged (`armed_while_pie_running`) -- the BeginPlay window has already passed for that session, which is precisely the failure this tool exists to avoid, so stop PIE, arm, then start PIE. It self-disarms on duration_seconds or max_samples (it can never leak a ticker) and the recorded samples survive until action="clear".

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | string | no | Optional: "start" (default) \| "status" \| "stop" \| "clear" \| "list". |
| `property_name` | string | no | Property to sample on the matched object. Required for "start" unless `properties` is given. |
| `properties` | array | no | Optional array of property names sampled TOGETHER, in the SAME tick, as one ROW. This is what answers correlation questions ("movement_mode changed in the same tick immersion crossed the threshold"), which N separate watches cannot: each would dedupe on its own clock and the columns would not line up. The row is the dedup unit -- if ANY field changes the whole row is recorded -- and each sample carries a `values` object with the per-property breakdown. With one property there is no `values` object. |
| `class_name` | string | no | Optional actor class filter (exact UClass name; a Blueprint class needs the "_C" suffix). At least one of class_name / actor_label is required for "start". |
| `actor_label` | string | no | Optional actor filter, matched against the editor label OR the object name. |
| `component` | string | no | Optional component name: sample the property on that component of the matched actor instead of on the actor. |
| `sample_interval_seconds` | number | no | Optional periodic sampling interval (default 0.1, min 0.01). |
| `duration_seconds` | number | no | Optional auto-disarm after this many real seconds (default 300; 0 = no time cap, disarms only on max_samples or an explicit stop). |
| `max_samples` | number | no | Optional hard cap on recorded samples (default 400). |
| `watch_id` | number | no | Target watch for "status" / "stop" / "clear" (omit = all of them). |

**Returns:** `{ action: string, watch_id?: int, armed?: bool, watches: [{ watch_id, property_name, class_name, actor_label, component, sample_interval_seconds, duration_seconds, max_samples, active, saw_pie_world, armed_while_pie_running, sample_count, elapsed_real_seconds, stop_reason, distinct_objects_seen, samples?: [{ phase, object_path, actor_label, value_text, value, elapsed_real_seconds, world_time_seconds, world, changed_from_previous }] }], identifies_writer: bool, sampling_only: bool, armed_pre_pie?: bool, pie_running?: bool, class_resolved?: bool, hint?: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }. The five world_* / net_mode / pie_instance fields identify the PIE world the ticker is sampling AT THE MOMENT OF THE CALL (all null / pie_instance -1 when no PIE session is running, which is the normal state right after arming).`
